judge_assessment.explanation: The arithmetic and the OCR explanation both hold: 4/0/7 -> 407, 600+0+5 = 605, 406 < 460, 308, 720, 3 hundreds + 0 tens + 9 ones + 4 more tens = 349, the ascending 308/380/830, and 700 > 70 are all correct, and there are exactly eight \problem bodies. But 'Zero placeholders are treated correctly in standard, expanded, and represented forms' overstates what was verified. The expanded form -- the named focus of this task -- is never machine-checked anywhere on the sheet. Problem 1 prints the chart answer AND 'Then finish the expanded form: __ + __ + __', four response slots in total, and verify.json id 1 carries one entry, h*100+t*10+n = 407. Problems 4(b) and 5(b) say 'Write the expanded form of 308 correctly, and write the number it makes' and 'Write the expanded form of 720 correctly ...', and each is covered only by the value (308, 720). So the '400 + 0 + 7' and '300 + 0 + 8' the whole worksheet is about are unverified. Two further gaps: problem 3 says 'Explain on the answer line which place makes the difference' and problem 8(b) says 'tell how you know', and neither is flagged manual although problems 4(a) and 5(a) ARE -- the same sheet treats the same demand two ways. And the Quick Answers bank prints '3. -' for a verified '<' and '8. 700, 70, -' for a verified '>'.

strengths_to_preserve: The two planted errors are computed from the slip rather than asserted: verify.json declares Jamal's trap as {'expr': 'h*100 + n*10', 'value': 380} -- literally the arithmetic of sliding the 8 into the tens place -- and Ruby's as {'expr': 'h*100 + t', 'value': 702}, counting the 2 as ones. That makes each planted wrong answer provably reachable and provably distinct from the right one.

Problem 6 makes the zero placeholder do work instead of just naming it: 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones plus 4 more tens is the one item where the empty place has to receive something, and 349 is only obtainable by respecting it.

Problem 8 pushes the same digit through two different places (7 hundreds versus 7 tens) so the comparison 700 > 70 cannot be answered by digit-matching -- the cleanest possible statement of what 'holds a place' means.

root_causes.description: Coverage is enforced per problem id, so a problem may print several response slots and satisfy the gate with one entry. Here the uncovered slots are precisely the task's focus: the expanded-form decompositions in problems 1, 4(b) and 5(b).
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 1 prints the chart value slot plus 'Then finish the expanded form: __ + __ + __'; verify.json id 1 has one entry (407).
Problem 4(b) 'Write the expanded form of 308 correctly, and write the number it makes' -> only 308 verified; the '300 + 0 + 8' string is not.
The task contract's focus is 'correcting a zero-placeholder error in expanded form', so the unverified slot is the target skill itself.

root_causes.description: Explanation prompts are flagged manual only when the author remembers; nothing enforces it, producing inconsistency inside a single worksheet.
evidence: verify.json ids 4 and 5 each carry a manual entry for 'Explain in words what Jamal/Ruby did wrong'.
Problem 3 ('Explain on the answer line which place makes the difference') and problem 8(b) ('tell how you know') carry only compare/eval entries.
final_response.md reports 'Two items are flagged for manual review', undercounting the sheet's four explanation prompts.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt routes relation strings through bare sympify, which raises, and returns '---' -- the same glyph used for manual-only rows.
evidence: verify.json id 3 is compare '<' (verified) and id 8's third entry is compare '>' (verified).

improvements.title: Verify the expanded-form decomposition, not just the number it makes
improvements.proposed_change: Move the SKILL.md coverage rule from per-problem-id to per-rendered-answer-slot and enforce it in tests/check_layout.py by counting \ansblank, \ansline and bare \underline{\hspace{...}} rules inside each \problem body against the expecteds bound to that id. For expanded-form items, require one entry per addend slot (400, 0, 7 for problem 1; 300, 0, 8 for problem 4b; 700, 20, 0 for problem 5b) so the zero placeholder itself is a checked value rather than an implicit consequence of the total.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem prints a value slot plus three expanded-form addend slots while verify.json supplies only the total: tests/check_layout.py must exit non-zero naming the uncovered slots. Passes today (problem 1 here has exactly that shape and built green); after the fix only the four-entry version passes.
improvements.expected_impact: A worksheet whose declared focus is expanded form stops shipping with the expanded form as its only unverified content, and a wrong '400 + 7' in the key could no longer pass unnoticed.
improvements.risk: Multi-addend entries make verify files longer and existing corpus files will fail until back-filled; the slot counter must not count the chart's digit boxes as response slots.

improvements.title: Flag problems 3 and 8(b) manual, as problems 4(a) and 5(a) already are
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate scanning each \problem body for explanation cues ('explain', 'tell how you know', 'say why', 'describe') that fails unless the problem id carries a manual entry, and derive the manual count in the delivery summary from verify.json. This sheet already contains the correct pattern twice, so the fix is enforcement, not new guidance.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with one problem containing 'Explain on the answer line which place makes the difference' and only a compare entry, and a second problem with the same prose plus a manual entry: the gate must fail the first and pass the second. Fails today.
improvements.expected_impact: A consistent manual-review count across a sheet, so the adult knows all four explanations need reading rather than two.
improvements.risk: False positives on narrative stems; restrict matching to imperative sentences and allow an author override.

improvements.title: Print '406 < 460' and '700 > 70' in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt before sympify and typeset them with the compared 'values'; use a distinct marker for manual-only rows so a dash always means 'a human must read this'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: a compare/relation entry must render the relation and never '---'. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Row 3 and the tail of row 8 regain their answers, and the bank stops implying two comparison problems were unchecked.
improvements.risk: Wider entries may reduce the bank's column count.

case_summary: A precise misconception sheet: both planted errors are declared with the arithmetic that produces them (300 + 80 = 380 from sliding the digit, 700 + 2 = 702 from mis-reading the 2 as ones), every value I recomputed is correct, and problems 6 and 8 make the zero placeholder consequential rather than decorative. The gap is that the task's own focus is the least-verified thing on the page -- the expanded-form slots in problems 1, 4(b) and 5(b) print blanks that no verify entry covers, so only the totals were ever checked. The sheet is also inconsistent about explanations, flagging two of four manual, and the Quick Answers bank drops the verified '<' in row 3 and the verified '>' in row 8.
